mainTopic: Learning the rules of ספק טומאה from סוטה, and questions on the exchange between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל about תרומה and כהונה.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that learns the laws of ספק טומאה (doubtful impurity) from the case of סוטה. First it completes a קל וחומר: a doubt about impurity is treated like a certainty. Since סוטה is the source, the details come from סוטה too. A סוטה case happens in a private place (רשות היחיד), and a סוטה is a person who can be asked questions (דעת לישאל). So a doubt about touching a שרץ makes something impure only under those same two conditions. In every other case the doubt is pure. The גמרא then turns to the exchange between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל in the ברייתא. It asks why רבי ישמעאל answered about כהונה when רבי עקיבא spoke about תרומה. It also asks where רבי עקיבא learns that a סוטה may not marry a כהן, and it begins to test the idea that no פסוק is needed.

steps.title: A doubt is treated like a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its קל וחומר: a case of ספק טומאה is treated like ודאי טומאה (certain impurity).
steps.simpleTranslation: [A doubtful case of impurity should be treated] like a certain case.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes a sentence that began on the previous page. The ברייתא concludes that a doubt about impurity is treated as if the impurity were certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ברייתא built a קל וחומר from סוטה: if a doubt makes a סוטה forbidden, a doubt about impurity should surely count too. The word כוודאי is the bottom line of that argument. The rest of the piece now explains where this rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a certainty: treated as if it definitely happened
A doubt: we don't know what happened
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

steps.confusionAlert: This word is the end of a sentence from the previous page. It is not a new statement on its own.

phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from the previous page: a doubtful case of impurity becomes like a certain one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the קל וחומר from סוטה that began on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A case of ספק טומאה is treated like ודאי טומאה.

steps.title: Only a doubt in a private domain counts
steps.stepSummary: Because the rule comes from סוטה, it is limited like סוטה: just as סוטה happens in a רשות היחיד, a doubt about touching a שרץ makes something impure only in a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the source you came from: just as סוטה is in a private domain, so too a doubt about a שרץ is impure only in a private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says the source itself limits the rule. A סוטה doubt happens in a private place, so ספק טומאה from a שרץ only counts in a private place too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we learned the rule from סוטה, we can only stretch it as far as סוטה goes. סוטה is about a woman who went into hiding with a man in a private place. So the first limit is: the doubt must arise in a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place you came from: from the very source of the rule
Private domain: a place where few people are around
A dead creeping animal, which makes things impure
A woman suspected of adultery after hiding alone with a man

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why many doubts of impurity in public places are treated as pure.

phrases.english: And from the place that you came from:
phrases.notes: He means: the same סוטה case that taught us the rule also sets its limits.

phrases.english: just as a sota is in a private domain,
so too a creeping animal is in a private domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule just proven by tying it to the details of its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספק טומאה from a שרץ is impure only when the doubt arises in a רשות היחיד.

steps.title: Only something that can be asked counts
steps.stepSummary: A second limit from סוטה: a סוטה is a person who can be asked what happened, so only something with דעת לישאל becomes impure from a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as a סוטה is something that has the understanding to be asked, so too a שרץ doubt counts only for something that has the understanding to be asked.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second condition taken from סוטה. The doubt only makes something impure if it involves someone or something that could be asked about what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה is a person who can be asked whether she sinned. So the rule only applies to things with דעת לישאל, which means a person, or an object that was with a person who could answer. Objects with no one aware, like an item lying alone, are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Understanding to be asked: able to answer questions about what happened
Just as ... so too: comparing one case to another
A thing or entity

phrases.english: is an entity that has the understanding to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁרֶץ דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל.
phrases.english: so too a creeping animal [case] is an entity that has the understanding to be asked.
phrases.notes: It's not the שרץ itself that has understanding. It means the thing that may have touched the שרץ.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the dead שרץ can be asked. The 'entity' is the person or object that may have become impure.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה סוֹטָה דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit from סוטה, next to the רשות היחיד limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספק טומאה applies only to an entity with דעת לישאל.

steps.title: The final rule for doubtful impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא puts both limits together: something with דעת לישאל is impure if the doubt was in a רשות היחיד and pure if it was in a רשות הרבים. Something without דעת לישאל is always pure in a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: something that can be asked, in a private domain, its doubt is impure; in a public domain, its doubt is pure. Something that cannot be asked, whether in a private or public domain, its doubt is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the practical rule that comes out of the two limits. It covers all four cases: private or public place, and able or unable to be asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubt is impure only when both conditions are met, like in סוטה: a private place and something that can be asked. If the doubt was in a public place, it is pure. If the thing cannot be asked, it is pure anywhere, because it is not like סוטה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And from here they said: introduces a rule based on what came before
Public domain: a place where many people are around
Its doubt is impure: we treat it as impure
Its doubt is pure: we treat it as pure

steps.whatToRemember: ספק טומאה is impure only when it is in a רשות היחיד AND involves something with דעת לישאל, just like סוטה. In any other case the doubt is pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for deciding doubts of impurity in practice.

phrases.english: an entity that has the understanding to be asked,
in the private domain, its doubt is impure;
in the public domain, its doubt is pure.
And one that does not have the understanding to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים —
phrases.english: whether in the private domain or in the public domain,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two limits from steps 2 and 3 into one practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A doubt is impure only for something with דעת לישאל in a רשות היחיד. A doubt in a רשות הרבים, or for something without דעת לישאל, is pure.

steps.title: Why does רבי ישמעאל answer about כהונה when רבי עקיבא spoke about תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי ישמעאל's reply does not seem to match what רבי עקיבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? רבי עקיבא said תרומה, and he answers him about כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's exchange. It asks why רבי ישמעאל's answer is about a different topic than the one רבי עקיבא raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא taught that a סוטה may not eat תרומה. רבי ישמעאל's response was about her being forbidden to marry into כהונה. A response is supposed to address what was said, so the mismatch needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן and his household may eat
The priesthood; here it means being allowed to marry a כהן
And he answers him / responds to him

phrases.english: and he answers him about the priesthood?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא תְּרוּמָה, וּמַהְדַּר לֵיהּ אִיהוּ כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ספק טומאה section, the גמרא returns to another part of the ברייתא and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exchange between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reply should address the speaker's point. רבי עקיבא spoke about תרומה, but רבי ישמעאל replied about כהונה.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that a סוטה is forbidden to a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: A second problem: רבי עקיבא gives no source for the rule that a סוטה may not marry a כהן. The גמרא starts to suggest that maybe no פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: according to רבי עקיבא, where does he learn כהונה from? And if you will say that כהונה does not need a פסוק...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question: what is רבי עקיבא's source for forbidding a סוטה to a כהן? It then begins to offer a possible answer, that no פסוק is needed. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will deal with that suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's source deals with תרומה, so his source for כהונה is missing. The phrase וכי תימא introduces an answer someone might give: the rule about כהונה does not need its own פסוק (it can be known some other way). The גמרא will test that answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional difficulty
From where does he know it? A request for a source
And if you will say; introduces a possible answer that the גמרא will examine
A פסוק (verse)

steps.confusionAlert: The words וכי תימא are not the גמרא's final answer. They introduce a suggestion that the גמרא is about to examine, and the step continues past this line.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כְּהוּנָּה מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And furthermore: according to Rabbi Akiva, from where does he derive the priesthood?
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a סוטה may not marry a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא כְּהוּנָּה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא,
phrases.english: And if you would say that the priesthood does not need a verse,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כְּהוּנָּה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This adds a second difficulty about the same exchange in the ברייתא, this time about רבי עקיבא's own position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's position that a סוטה is forbidden to a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule needs a source. רבי עקיבא's source covers תרומה, so nothing is given for כהונה. The suggestion that כהונה needs no פסוק is raised so it can be examined next.
